I would keep it simple and stay with the system I trust most in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits our local climate, our water conditions, and the way I already know how to manage fields. I am 52, my schooling is not high, so I would not gamble on a complicated cash-crop plan that needs tight market timing or delicate field management. I would rather run a steady grain rotation, use improved seed, control fertilizer costs, irrigate at the key stages, and do pest sprays only when they matter. Because you did not give my land area, I will assume I am managing 10 mu total, with the full 10 mu going into winter wheat first and then the same 10 mu into summer maize after wheat harvest. I would plough before wheat to make a solid seedbed, then use rotary tillage before maize to save time after the wheat comes off. I would aim for stable yield instead of chasing the highest possible output, because for me the safer decision is the one that protects grain, labor, and cash flow.
